name: SSH Brute Force Attack
short_description: Use Hydra and Metasploit to crack weak SSH passwords.
description: Many systems still use weak or default passwords. This lesson teaches you to use Hydra (fast) and Metasploit (integrated) to brute force SSH credentials. The target has intentionally weak passwords: root/toor and user/password.

steps.title: Verify SSH is running
steps.explanation: Confirm the SSH service is accessible.

steps.title: Try Hydra first (faster)
steps.explanation: Hydra tries each password in the wordlist. -t 4 means 4 parallel threads. This is faster than Metasploit for brute forcing.

steps.title: Alternative: Use Metasploit
steps.explanation: Metasploit's scanner is slower but integrates with the database.

steps.title: Load the SSH login scanner
steps.explanation: This is an auxiliary module (scanner), not an exploit.

steps.title: Set a small password list
steps.explanation: Point to a wordlist. Smaller lists are faster.

steps.title: Run the brute force
steps.explanation: This will try each password until it finds one that works.

steps.title: Connect with found credentials
steps.explanation: Use the discovered password (toor) to log in.

success_criteria: Hydra or Metasploit finds the password 'toor' for root, and you can SSH in with those credentials.
next_steps: Use 'sessions' in Metasploit to see if it created a session
